w10_T4_004019: Sarah and Mike are saving for a trip. Sarah starts with 194 dollars. In the morning, she spends 51 dollars on supplies. By afternoon, her money is multiplied by 5 through an unexpected bonus payment. By evening, she adds 39 dollars from a gift. Finally, she pays a 299-dollar bill. How much money does Sarah end up with?
w10_T4_004025: Alex is tallying his garden expenses in minutes, which he will later convert to hours. He starts with 233 minutes of work time. He multiplies his effort by 5 days of work, giving him 1165 units. He then loses 1068 minutes due to weather delays. The next day he gains 3 minutes of extra work time. Finally, he adds 11 more minutes. How much total time, in minutes, did Alex accumulate?
w10_T4_004026: A factory produces shelf units. One shelf begins with 34 items. After a morning shift, 25 items are removed for quality inspection. The remaining items are then multiplied by 7 because each will be packaged into sets of 7. Next, 71 more items arrive from another line. Finally, the entire batch is multiplied by 8 for distribution across warehouses. How many items end up on that shelf after all these changes?
w10_T4_004028: Jordan and Casey are running a catering business. Jordan starts with 23 portions of salad. On day 1, the recipe is tripled, making 69 portions. On day 2, the batch is doubled to 138 portions. On day 3, it is multiplied by 7 to reach 966 portions. Finally, 59 more portions are added for a last-minute event. How many portions does Jordan end up with?
w10_T4_004030: Emma has 115 dollars in her bakery fund. She doubles her investment by getting a loan, now having 230 dollars. She then spends 200 dollars on ingredients, leaving 30 dollars. Next, she loses 18 dollars to spoilage. Finally, she adds 23 dollars from a small sale. Her partner has 50 dollars. How much money does Emma have at the end?
w10_T4_004033: A library shelf starts with 36 books. During the morning, 52 more books are added. By afternoon, another 32 books arrive. By evening, 58 more books are shelved. However, 62 books are then returned to the storage room. The neighboring shelf has 100 books. How many books remain on this shelf?
w10_T4_004040: Lisa has 13 candies. She receives 41 more, bringing her to 54 candies. She then shares them equally among 6 friends, leaving each with 9 candies and her with 9 candies (54 divided by 6). She keeps 4 groups worth, giving her 36 candies. Finally, she eats 8 candies. How many candies does Lisa have remaining?
w10_T4_004052: Tom starts his chocolate business with 232 units of inventory. He multiplies by 8 over a week (1856 units). He then divides by half (sharing with a partner), leaving him 928. He loses 467 to spoilage, leaving 461. He gains 19 more units. He multiplies sales by 8 for a wholesale order (3688 units). Finally, he pays out 2900 in costs. How much inventory value remains?
w10_T4_004054: A community garden starts with 62 plants. In the morning, they add 44 more. By afternoon, 23 new seedlings arrive. This total is tripled by evening to prepare for expansion (261 plants). Then 24 specimens are donated to neighbors. Finally, 42 more are purchased. How many plants does the garden have now?
w10_T4_004056: A fundraiser starts with 94 dollars. Donors add 75 dollars in the morning, then 67 more at noon, then 28 by evening (totaling 264 dollars). The amount is then tripled for a matching grant program (792 dollars). It is tripled again by a foundation (2376 dollars). How much money has the fundraiser accumulated?
w10_T4_004069: A construction project begins with 75 minutes of material prep time. It gains 32 additional minutes, totaling 107. This is multiplied by 5 teams working in parallel (535 min-hours). Then 50 minutes are added for cleanup prep. The total effort is multiplied by 8 days (4280). Then 16 more inspection minutes are added, then 25 more. Another site has 30 minutes of work. How many total minutes of work time are recorded?
w10_T4_004079: Maya and David run a printing business. They start with 138 sheets. They multiply by 3 (414 sheets). They then add 31 printed sheets. This total is multiplied by 4 for a bulk order (1780 sheets). Finally, a client orders all 1695 sheets, leaving them 85. How many sheets does Maya's inventory show?
w10_T4_004084: Josh starts a candle-making business with 16 units. He multiplies by 5 (80 units), then by 8 (640 units). He adds 23 new units (663 units). The batch is then multiplied by 5 for shipment to stores (3315 units). His partner has 100 units. How many candles does Josh have to ship?
w10_T4_004088: A farm has 133 sheep. They double (266), then double again (532), then double once more (1064). Finally, 4 more sheep are added (1068). The herd is then multiplied by 9 for a breeding program calculation (9612 estimated sheep). How many sheep are projected in the calculation?
w10_T4_004092: A software company starts with 221 users. They multiply by 5 (1105), then by 5 again (5525). They lose 3094 users in a system migration (2431). Finally, the remaining users are multiplied by 9 for a forecast model (21879). How many users does the forecast predict?
w10_T4_004093: Sofia starts a jewel-making business with 153 pieces. She multiplies production by 6 (918). She loses 650 pieces to quality control (268). This total is multiplied by 5 (1340). A major defect costs 573 pieces. Morning work was significant, afternoon saw losses, evening showed the final inventory. How many finished pieces does Sofia have?
w10_T4_004105: Ren and Jo are gardening partners. Ren starts with 159 seeds. He multiplies by 5 (795), then by 7 (5565). He divides by 5 to share equally (1113). He adds 74 more seeds. Jo has 500 seeds. How many seeds does Ren have for planting?
w10_T4_004109: A factory processes 91 kilos of material daily. On day 1, it multiplies by 7 (637). On day 2, 58 more kilos arrive (695). On day 3, 34 kilos are removed (661). On day 4, 245 kilos are lost to spillage (416). On day 5, output is multiplied by 8 (3328). Finally, 2837 kilos are shipped. Morning shifts were heavy, afternoon saw losses, evening brought shipments. What is the remaining material?
w10_T4_004114: Blake and Rivers manage a grain storage. Blake starts with 146 sacks. He multiplies by 8 (1168). He adds 20 sacks (1188). He loses 106 to pests (1082). The entire amount is divided in half to separate storage (541 per location). Rivers manages another location. How many sacks does Blake's first storage have?
w10_T4_004115: A bakery starts with 160 loaves. They multiply by 7 (1120), then by 5 (5600). They add 29 (5629). A major recall removes 2931 loaves (2698). They multiply by 5 for restocking (13490). They add 76 more. Morning baking was heavy, afternoon saw recalls, evening involved restocking. How many loaves are ready for sale?
w10_T4_004118: A bookstore starts with 164 books. They add 72 (236). They remove 62 damaged ones (174). They multiply by 5 for display purposes (870). They add 16 more (886). They lose 644 during an inventory error (242). Finally, they multiply by 6 for ordering (1452). How many books are in the reorder calculation?
w10_T4_004121: Marcus has 215 dollars in savings. He receives 8 more (223). He withdraws 215 for bills (8). He divides by 4 to allocate for weekly expenses (2 per week). He loses 1 dollar to fees (1). He adds 14 from a refund (15). Half of a dozen dollars would be 6. What is Marcus's final balance?
w10_T4_004123: A factory starts with 197 units of raw material. They lose 6 to defects (191). They multiply by 9 for production scheduling (1719). They lose 878 in processing (841). They multiply by 6 for supply planning (5046). They lose 1323 to shrinkage. How much material remains in inventory?
w10_T4_004126: Pedro and Anna run a farm. Pedro starts with 37 acres. He adds 12 acres (49). He adds 53 more (102). He adds 74 more (176). He divides in half to separate crops (88 per section). He multiplies by 6 for yield calculations (528 units). He loses 147 to erosion. Anna manages twice as many acres total. How many acres does Pedro's calculation show?
w10_T4_004129: A storage facility has 228 items. In the morning, it gains 6 (234). By afternoon, 43 are sold (191). By evening, 90 more are sold (101). Finally, 60 more are removed for returns (41). How many items remain in storage?
